content.thinking:
I'm checking each claim in the draft against what the sources support. The account-page failure, the divide-by-zero cause, and the peak error rate all look backed up, so I'm moving on to the cost estimate in claim four.

I'm finishing the review of the remaining claims: the paging point is fine, the feature-flag revert is still in place, and the demo user closed the incident before Argus judged the revert, with the timing checking out. The last claim about the flag and the checkout team is also supported, so the whole draft holds up.

supported.quote: On io-shop, account pages failed for some shoppers over {duration}.
rows: What a reader saw: Shoppers' account pages failed

supported.quote: Turning on a new monthly-spending feature made those pages run a calculation that tried to divide by zero.
rows: Why, in plain words: Turning on a new monthly-spending feature...

supported.quote: At the worst minute, {peak_error_rate} of requests failed.
rows: Requests failing at the worst minute: 40.5% {peak_error_rate}

supported.quote: Argus estimates the incident cost the shop {customer_loss} in takings.
rows: What it cost the shop in takings (estimated by Argus): 5,422.30 USD {customer_loss}

supported.quote: Nobody was paged, so no on-call responder was called in.
rows: Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one.

supported.quote: To end it, Argus reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature, and that change is still in place.
rows: Argus: reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature - not judged by Argus (demo user resolved it first), still in place

supported.quote: A demo user then closed the incident from the Argus UI before Argus had judged whether the revert worked.
The demo user noted that they had kept the flag off and told the checkout team.
rows: demo user: resolved it from the Argus UI - "kept the flag off and told the checkout team"
